question.text: If $z_1$ and $z_2$ be two roots of the equation $z^2+a z+b=0, a^2 \lt 4 b$, then the origin, $z_1$ and $z_2$ form an equilateral triangle if

solution.text: Hint: Here, $z_1+z_2=-a$ and $z_1 z_2=b$ $z_2=z_1 e^{i \pi / 3}=z_1\left(\cos \frac{\pi}{3}+i \sin \frac{\pi}{3}\right)=z_1\left(\frac{1}{2}+i \cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$ $\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 2 z_2-z_1=\sqrt{3} \cdot i z_1 \Rightarrow\left(2 z_2-z_1\right)^2=-3 z_1^2 \Rightarrow 4 z_2^2+4 z_1^2=4 z_1 z_2 \Rightarrow z_1^2+z_2^2=z_1 z_2 \\ & \Rightarrow\left(z_1+z_2\right)^2-2 z_1 z_2=z_1 z_2 \Rightarrow a^2-2 b=b \Rightarrow a^2=3 b\end{aligned}$
